qa: What does a holistic practitioner do?

A holistic practitioner looks at the whole person – body, mind, emotions and lifestyle – rather than a single symptom. Depending on their training they may offer bodywork, energy work, coaching, nutrition advice or spiritual guidance, usually alongside rather than instead of medical care.
How much does a session with a holistic practitioner cost?

Prices vary by therapy, location and experience. In Ireland and the UK a one-hour session typically costs between €50 and €100 (£40–£90). Many practitioners offer a reduced first session or a free introductory call.
How many sessions will I need?

It depends on what you are working on. Many people notice a difference after one to three sessions; ongoing issues may need a regular series. A good holistic practitioner will suggest a plan and review it with you rather than pushing a large package up front.

qa: How long does a sound bath last?
Most group sessions last 60 to 90 minutes, including a short introduction and time to settle and come back afterwards. The sound itself usually lasts 30 to 60 minutes.
Can I fall asleep during a sound bath?
Yes, and many people do. Even if you drift off, your body is resting deeply. Some people prefer to stay awake by lying with a cushion under their knees and keeping their hands on their belly.
How often should I go to a sound bath?
There is no rule. Some people join a sound bath monthly as a reset; others go weekly during stressful periods. Notice how you feel in the days afterwards and let that guide you.

qa: Is Reiki safe?

Reiki is gentle and non-invasive, and it is generally considered safe for most people. It should never replace medical diagnosis or treatment. If you have a health condition, tell your practitioner and keep seeing your doctor.
Do I need to believe in Reiki for it to work?
No belief is required. Many people come to Reiki sceptical and simply notice that they feel calmer and more rested afterwards. An open mind and a willingness to relax are enough.
How often should I have Reiki?
Some people book Reiki once for a reset; others choose weekly sessions for a month during a difficult period, then monthly. Your practitioner can suggest a rhythm that suits you.

qa: How long should breathwork for beginners take each day?

Five minutes a day is plenty when you start. Breathwork for beginners works best little and often: a few minutes in the morning and a few minutes before sleep will do more than one long session a week.
Which technique should I start with?
Begin with belly breathing and the long exhale (breathe in for 4, out for 6). They are gentle, easy to remember and suitable for almost everyone. Add box breathing once these feel natural.
Is it normal to feel dizzy?

Light-headedness usually means you are breathing too deeply or too fast. Slow down, breathe more softly through your nose and return to your normal breath. Stop if you feel unwell and speak to your doctor if it continues.

qa: Do I have to talk in a healing circle?
No. You can always pass. Listening is a full and valued way of taking part, and many people simply listen in their first healing circle.
Is a healing circle the same as group therapy?

No. A healing circle is a space for peer support and community care, guided by a facilitator. Group therapy is led by a qualified therapist and works with clinical goals. If you need therapy, a good facilitator will encourage you to seek it.
How many people are in a healing circle?
Most circles have between six and twenty people. Smaller circles feel more intimate; larger ones can be powerful for ceremonies and celebrations.

qa: What is the easiest meditation for beginners?
Breath awareness is the easiest meditation for beginners: sit comfortably, notice your breath and gently come back to it each time your mind wanders. Five minutes is enough.
Should I meditate in the morning or at night?
Either works. Mornings are often quieter and help set the tone for the day; an evening practice can help you unwind before sleep. The best time is the one you can keep.
When will I notice a difference?
Many people feel calmer straight after a session. Longer-term changes, such as reacting less strongly to stress, usually build over several weeks of regular practice.

qa: What does holistic wellbeing mean?

Holistic wellbeing means looking after your physical, mental, emotional and spiritual health together, because each affects the others. It focuses on balance and prevention as well as on solving problems.
Where should I start with holistic wellbeing?
Start with sleep, daily movement and a few minutes of quiet each day. These three foundations support everything else and need no special equipment.
Is holistic wellbeing an alternative to medical care?
No. Holistic wellbeing complements medical care. Keep seeing your GP for health concerns and use holistic practices to support your overall balance.

qa: How long should my first wellness retreat be?
A weekend wellness retreat of two or three nights is a good first step. It is long enough to unwind properly and short enough to fit around work and family.
Can I go to a wellness retreat on my own?
Absolutely. Many guests travel alone, and retreats are designed to be welcoming. Shared meals and group sessions make it easy to connect, while free time lets you enjoy your own company.
How much does a wellness retreat cost?
Day retreats can start from around €60–€120, while residential retreats in Ireland and the UK often range from €250 to €1,000 or more depending on length, accommodation and programme.
